title: Chapter 44: Reviews
html:
“Current Affection Levels:

“Qin Guoheng (Lingering Spirit): Unfamiliar (You cannot yet be considered friends; he helped you out of kindness.)

“Du Ruoshui (Lingering Spirit): Unfamiliar

“Qin Munan (Lingering Spirit): Unfamiliar

“Qin Xiaoxiao (Baleful Specter): Slightly Favorable (You have attracted her attention. To her, you are a little closer than a stranger.)

“Zhang Ya (Red Specter): Crazy About You (You are unique to her. She likes you—but only after you are dead.)

“To raise Affection, expose them to visitors’ fear and other intense negative emotions, give them items containing Malice Points, or complete their Bloody Heart Missions.

“Once Affection reaches a sufficient level, they may choose to follow your requests.

“Warning: Only specters with exceptionally deep malice and dark histories can issue Bloody Heart Missions. Completing one will greatly increase Affection and may persuade the specter to help with a request that does not violate its own will.”

The new feature gave Chen Ge a clearer picture of his supernatural “friends.” He took out the smallest doll. Physically, she looked no different from the others, but the black phone classified her separately: among the Ping An family, she alone was a Baleful Specter.

You count as a Baleful Specter?

Chen Ge poked Xiaoxiao’s cheek. Dangling in his hand, the doll somehow gave the impression of an indignant kitten trying very hard to look threatening.

I suppose that explains a few things.

If Qin Xiaoxiao represented the gentler end of the Baleful Specter category, Zhang Ya seemed to exist at the opposite extreme. More importantly, this was the first time Chen Ge had seen the classification “Red Specter.”

What exactly separates a normal Baleful Specter from a Red Specter?

He tapped Zhang Ya’s name. The interface immediately turned a deep, ominous red.

“Accept Zhang Ya’s Bloody Heart Mission? Warning: This mission carries significant danger.”

The warning alone was enough to make cold sweat bead on Chen Ge’s forehead.The phone said only specters with exceptionally deep malice and dark histories can issue Bloody Heart Missions. Of course my first draw would give me one of those.

His next thought was considerably less charitable.I would happily return this kind of luck.

On the off chance Zhang Ya could somehow hear him, he wisely kept that opinion to himself.

Crazy about me—but only after I’m dead? That is a terrifying definition of affection.

After closing the interface, the mirror entity suddenly seemed much less intimidating by comparison. That did not mean Chen Ge intended to ignore it. If anything, he was more determined than ever to remove the threat before it endangered another visitor.

My Friends from the Other Side gave him another glimpse of the black phone’s long-term design. It seemed intended to become the foundation for recruiting supernatural employees as the Haunted House expanded. With every unlocked feature, Chen Ge became more curious about where the system was leading him.

Once he understood the new tab, he turned to his other reward: Yin Yang Vision.

Nightmare Mission rewards tended to change Chen Ge himself. He stared down the dark corridor. Apart from being able to see more clearly in low light, he could not immediately tell what Yin Yang Vision had done.

Maybe it only activates under the right conditions, like Mortician’s Makeup.

He lifted a random mirror fragment and studied his reflection. His eyes looked exactly as they always had.

The description says Yin Yang Vision should let me see things ordinary people cannot, but…

He raised Xiaoxiao to eye level. All he saw was an ordinary rag doll.Am I using it wrong, or does it require some specific condition?

After several fruitless experiments, Chen Ge put the question aside. His limbs had stiffened during the ritual, so he stretched, found a dry place to sit, and began reviewing the recording.

After everything I went through, I at least deserve some useful publicity out of it.

He uploaded a short version of the footage to the supernatural forum. It was around four in the morning, so he expected little response. A comment appeared almost immediately.

“Is this another ghost game? Did something actually appear in that bathroom?”

The commenter was the forum moderator. After a moment’s thought, Chen Ge added a brief note explaining that the footage came from a supernatural experiment and deliberately omitted the ritual’s steps. He retitled the post: “What Appeared Beside Me During the Deep Water Ritual?”

Within minutes, the comments began pouring in. Chen Ge’s previous post had earned him a following, and some users were apparently being dragged awake by friends just to watch the new clip.

“Absolutely not. Whatever you were doing in that bathroom, keep the instructions to yourself.”

“This one feels even stranger than your last video.”

“What is that shadow beside the tub? Please tell me that is an effect.”

“Did you notice anything unusual while you were filming? That thing looks like it is watching you.”

One commenter launched into a long explanation about bathrooms, Yin energy, and traditional geomancy. The theory was impossible to verify, but it fit the forum’s usual mixture of folklore and speculation.

“Whatever the ritual was, nobody should copy it just because it showed up in a ghost video.”

A few replies tried to provide background on similar folklore. Chen Ge skimmed them but, as before, chose not to argue with anyone. Instead, he returned to editing the footage.

He removed the most distressing part of the encounter and kept the section where the shadow became visible. The shorter cut preserved the supernatural reveal without showing everything that had happened.

He uploaded the edited clip under the title “The Shadow That Appeared During Deep Water.”

His followers were notified as soon as it went live, and several people commented before watching the entire clip.

“Another bathroom video? I thought we agreed mirrors were enough.”

“The title sounds dramatic. There had better actually be a shadow this time.”

“Public service announcement: watch the video; do not copy whatever the host was doing.”

“I take back my complaint. What is that thing beside the tub? Get it off my screen!”
